title: Ταῦρος καὶ αἶγες ἄγριαι
titleEn: The Bull and the Wild Goats
part: The Bull and the Wild Goats (Chambry 332)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 332. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« », [ ] for words Chambry deletes as interpolated). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ταῦρος διωκόμενος ὑπὸ λέοντος κατέφυγεν εἴς τι σπήλαιον, ἐν ᾧ ἦσαν αἶγες ἄγριαι.
sentences.tr: Tauros diōkomenos hypo leontos katephygen eis ti spēlaion, en hōi ēsan aiges agriai.
sentences.l: A bull being pursued by a lion fled for refuge into a certain cave, in which there were wild goats.

sentences.t: Τυπτόμενος δὲ ὑπ’ αὐτῶν καὶ κερατιζόμενος ἔφη· « Ἀλλ’ οὐχ ὑμᾶς φοβούμενος ἀνέχομαι, τὸν δὲ πρὸ τοῦ στομίου ἑστῶτα [λέοντα]. »
sentences.tr: Typtomenos de hyp’ autōn kai keratizomenos ephē· « All’ ouch hymas phoboumenos anechomai, ton de pro tou stomiou hestōta [leonta]. »
sentences.l: And being struck by them and butted with their horns, he said: « But it is not fearing you that I hold out, but the [lion] standing before the mouth. »
sentences.i: And as they struck and gored him he said: « It is not from fear of you that I bear this, but of the one standing before the mouth of the cave. »
sentences.n: φοβούμενος governs both ὑμᾶς and τὸν … ἑστῶτα, and the whole weight of the answer falls on the second: what he endures inside is nothing beside what waits outside. Chambry prints [λέοντα] in square brackets — his mark for a word he judges a later insertion and deletes; on his reading the participle ἑστῶτα already carried the sense and the name of the lion was added afterwards. The bracket is kept in the literal line and dropped in the idiomatic one. στόμιον is the 'mouth', the narrow entrance of the cave.

sentences.t: Οὕτω πολλοὶ διὰ φόβον τῶν κρειττόνων καὶ τὰς ἐκ τῶν ἡττόνων ὕβρεις ὑπομένουσιν.
sentences.tr: Houtō polloi dia phobon tōn kreittonōn kai tas ek tōn hēttonōn hybreis hypomenousin.
sentences.l: Thus many, through fear of the stronger, endure even the outrages that come from the weaker.
sentences.n: κρείττων and ἥττων are the comparatives 'stronger' and 'weaker' used as nouns, of the more and the less powerful. καί before τὰς … ὕβρεις is 'even'.
